title: Pass by address (part 2)
recap: A pointer passed by value can be locally reseated without changing the caller's pointer. A reference to that pointer permits intentional reseating of the caller's pointer variable.
Address management and pointee mutation are separate operations. This function changes the chosen object without changing the values stored in either object.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement redirect(active,replacement). active is a reference to the caller's pointer variable: make that pointer store replacement, including nullptr. Do not modify either pointed-to integer. This differs from changing only a local copy of a pointer.
